# Process relevant training text into jsonl format for doccano

Functions to process / prepare text into jsonl format

```{r process_text_to_jsonl_fns}

# generic function to set json/jsonl file name
set_file_name <- function(date = Sys.getenv("RUN_TAG"),
                          # format(Sys.Date(), 
                          #        "%b %d %Y"), # get today's date in format "Nov 4 2024"
                          file_type,
                          paper_set = "training",
                          article_section) {
  
  file_name <-
  paste0("output/doccano/",
         paper_set, "_",
         article_section, "_",
         stringr::str_replace_all(date, " ", "_"),
         ".", file_type)
  
  return(file_name)
  
}

# for e.g. 
set_file_name(file_type = "jsonl", 
              article_section = "title")
 

# read/load relevant sentences from a section (abstracts, methods, results, intros) for a set of PMIDs
# won't work for titles 
read_section_sentences <- function(section,
                                   pmids) {
  
  
    stopifnot(section %in% c("abstracts",
                           "methods",
                           "results",
                           "intros")
            )

  sentences_path <- here::here(paste0(
   "output", "/",
   section, "/",
   section, "_sentences", "/"
  ))
  
  stopifnot(dir.exists(sentences_path))

  sentences_files <- list.files(sentences_path,
                                pattern = "*.json",
                                full.names = FALSE
  ) |>
    sort()

  sentences_pmids <-
  stringr::str_extract(sentences_files,
                           pattern = "^\\d+(?=_)")

  sentences_files <- sentences_files[sentences_pmids %in% pmids]

  sentences <- sapply(sentences_files,
                    function(file) {
                      json_data <- fromJSON(here::here(paste0(sentences_path,
                                                              file)))

                      sentences_lines <- json_data[json_data != ""]

                    }
  )

  return(sentences)

}


set_entrez_key(Sys.getenv('NCBI_API_KEY'))

get_pubmed_titles <- function(pmids, 
                                 batch_size = 200, 
                                 verbose = TRUE) {
  
  n <- length(pmids)
  
  titles <- setNames(rep("MISSING", 
                            n), 
                        pmids
                        )  # initialize result
  
  # Split PMIDs into batches
  batches <- split(pmids, 
                   ceiling(seq_along(pmids)/batch_size)
                   )
  
  for(i in seq_along(batches)) {
    
    batch_pmids <- batches[[i]]
    
    if(verbose) message(sprintf("Fetching batch %d of %d (%d PMIDs)...", 
                                i, 
                                length(batches), 
                                length(batch_pmids)
                                )
                        )
    
    # Fetch XML
    xml_data <- entrez_fetch(db = "pubmed", 
                             id = paste(batch_pmids, 
                                        collapse = ","), 
                             rettype = "xml", 
                             parsed = FALSE
                             )
    
    doc <- read_xml(xml_data)
    articles <- xml_find_all(doc, ".//PubmedArticle")
    
    for(article in articles) {
      
      pmid_node <- xml_find_first(article, 
                                  ".//PMID")
      
      pmid <- xml_text(pmid_node)
      
      
      title_nodes <- xml_find_all(article, 
                                     ".//MedlineCitation/Article/ArticleTitle")
      
      if(length(title_nodes) > 0) {
        titles[pmid] <- paste(xml_text(title_nodes), 
                                 collapse = " ")
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(titles)
}


section_to_jsonl <- function(section,
                             pmids,
                             paper_set = "training",
                             run_tag = Sys.getenv("RUN_TAG")) {

  stopifnot(section %in% c("title",
                           "abstracts",
                           "methods",
                           "results",
                           "intros")
            )

  pmids <- unique(as.character(pmids))

  sentences <- if (section == "title") {
    get_pubmed_titles(pmids)
  } else {
    read_section_sentences(section, pmids)
  }

  json_list_sentences <-
    purrr::imap(sentences,
                function(sentences,
                         file_name) {
                  
                  if(section == "title") {
                     
                     df <- data.frame(source_file = "title",
                                      text = sentences,
                                      pubmed_id = file_name)
                  } else {

                     df <- data.frame(source_file = file_name,
                                      text = sentences)
                     
                     df <- mutate(df,
                               pubmed_id = stringr::str_extract(source_file,
                                                                pattern = "^\\d+(?=_)"
                                                                )
                               )
                  }
                  
                  df  <- mutate(df,
                                label = list(list()))

                  return(df)
                }
    )

  json_file = here::here(set_file_name(file_type = "json",
                                       paper_set = paper_set,
                                       article_section = section))


  jsonl_file = here::here(set_file_name(file_type = "jsonl",
                                        paper_set = paper_set,
                                        article_section = section))
  
  writeLines(toJSON(json_list_sentences,
                    auto_unbox = TRUE,
                    pretty = TRUE),
             json_file)

  json_data <- fromJSON(json_file,
                        simplifyVector = FALSE)

  json_rows <- unlist(json_data,
                      recursive = FALSE)

  # Open connection to JSONL file
  con <- file(jsonl_file, "w")

  # Loop over each element (object) and write as one line
  for (i in seq_along(json_rows)) {
    writeLines(toJSON(json_rows[[i]],
                      auto_unbox = TRUE),
               con)
  }

  close(con)
  
  print(paste0("JSONL file created for section: ", 
               section, " at: ", 
               fs::path_rel(jsonl_file,
                            start = here::here())
  ))

}

```

### Combine training examples into a single jsonl file

Concatenate training examples, and deduplicate based on pubmed_id and text, keeping the first occurrence of each unique combination, and reassigning ids.)

deduplicate is needed because in many cases where methods, results and introduction sections can't be identified from the xml file, the whole text is used as a fallback, which can lead to duplicate sentences across sections.

```{bash combine_training_examples, eval =FALSE}

cd output/doccano

# combine training examples into a single jsonl file
# create new sentence id numbers 
jq -c  '.' \
  training_title_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  training_abstracts_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  training_methods_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  training_results_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  training_intros_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
| jq -c -s 'to_entries | map(.value + {orig_id: .value.id, id: (.key + 1)}) | .[]' \
  > combined_training_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

# add source_section field based on source_file 
# source_section identifies the section of the article from which the sentence was extracted, e.g. title, abstract, methods, results, introduction, or full text (unknown section)
jq '
  . + {
    source_section:
      (if (.source_file | test("main"; "i")) then "full text (unknown section)"
       elif (.source_file | test("methods"; "i")) then "methods"
       elif (.source_file | test("results"; "i")) then "results"
       elif (.source_file | test("abstract"; "i")) then "abstract"
       elif (.source_file | test("title"; "i")) then "title"
       elif (.source_file | test("intro"; "i")) then "introduction"
       else null
       end)
  }
' combined_training_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_training_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl
  
# deduplicate combined training examples based on pubmed_id and text, keeping the first occurrence of each unique combination, and reassigning ids
jq -c -s '
  reduce .[] as $r ({seen: {}, out: []};
    ($r.pubmed_id + "\u0000" + $r.text) as $k
    | if .seen[$k] then . else .seen[$k] = true | .out += [$r] end)
  | .out
  | to_entries | map(.value + {orig_id: .value.id, id: (.key + 1)}) | .[]
' combined_training_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_training_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

# remove source_file and orig_id fields from combined_training_dedup.jsonl
jq -c 'del(.source_file)' combined_training_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_training_dedup_simple_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

jq -c 'del(.orig_id)' combined_training_dedup_simple_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_training_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

rm combined_training_dedup_simple_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl
rm combined_training_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

wc -l combined_training_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl combined_training_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

rm combined_training_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

```

```{bash basic_initial_annot}

# initial annotation of combined training examples
wc -l output/doccano/combined_training_dedup_${RUN_TAG}_annotated.jsonl

```

## Reduce/simplify training set

```{bash reduce_training_set}

cd output/doccano

# separate into examples without labels and examples with labels

IN=combined_training_dedup_${RUN_TAG}_annotated.jsonl

# At least one G_COHORT label
jq -c 'select((.label // []) | length > 0)' "$IN" > combined_training_annotated_with_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

# No labels
jq -c 'select((.label // []) | length == 0)' "$IN" > combined_training_annotated_no_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

wc -l combined_training_annotated_with_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
      combined_training_annotated_no_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
      "$IN"

# convert to json
for f in combined_training_annotated_with_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl combined_training_annotated_no_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl; do
  jq -s '.' "$f" > "${f%.jsonl}.json"
done      

jq -s 'map(.text)' \
combined_training_annotated_with_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_training_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json

jq -s 'map(.text)' \
combined_training_annotated_no_labels_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl  > combined_training_non_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json

```

#### Identify hard negatives (non-cohort sentences that are similar to cohort sentences)

Firstly, let's identify these by grep search of annotated entities. 

```{r identify_negs_by_grep}

annotated_training_sentences <- stream_in(file(here::here(
  paste0("output/doccano/combined_training_annotated_with_labels_",
         Sys.getenv("RUN_TAG"), 
         ".jsonl"))
  )
)

annotated_training_sentences_long <- annotated_training_sentences |>
  mutate(label = map(label, ~{
    if (length(.x) == 0) return(NULL)
    as.data.frame(.x) |>
      setNames(c("start", "end", "label"))
  })) |>
  tidyr::unnest(label, keep_empty = T) |>
  mutate(across(c(start, end), as.integer))

annotated_training_sentences_entities <-
annotated_training_sentences_long |> 
  mutate(entity_text = stringr::str_sub(text, 
                                        start + 1, 
                                        end)) |>
  mutate(entity_text = ifelse(is.na(entity_text), 
                              "", 
                              entity_text))

grep_entities <-
annotated_training_sentences_entities |>
  # order grep_entities by length, and then alphabetically
  dplyr::arrange(nchar(entity_text), entity_text) |>
  pull(entity_text) |>
  unique()

length(grep_entities)

grep_entities_pattern <- paste0("\\b(", 
                                paste(str_escape(grep_entities), 
                                      collapse = "|"), 
                                ")\\b")

annotated_training_sentences_no_labels <- stream_in(file(here::here(
  paste0("output/doccano/combined_training_annotated_no_labels_",
         Sys.getenv("RUN_TAG"), 
         ".jsonl"))
  )
)

matched_sentences <- annotated_training_sentences_no_labels |>
                     dplyr::filter(
                       str_detect(text, 
                                  pattern = grep_entities_pattern)
                     )
                       
matched_sentences |>
  nrow()

json_file = here::here(set_file_name(file_type = "json", 
                                     article_section = "hard_negatives_matched_grep"))

writeLines(toJSON(matched_sentences,
                  auto_unbox = TRUE,
                  pretty = TRUE),
           json_file)

```

Secondly, let's identify hard negatives by sentence embeddings and cosine similarity.

```{bash identify_negs_by_embeddings}

source  spacyr_venv/bin/activate

doccano_dir=output/doccano

python3 code/extract_text/sentence_embeddings.py \
        --label "Combined (title, abstracts, methods, results)" \
        --output "training_hard_negatives_semantic_similarity_${RUN_TAG}.json" \
        --cohort_path "output/doccano/combined_training_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json" \
        --non_cohort_path "output/doccano/combined_training_non_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json" \
        --figure_save_path "output/doccano/combined_training_sentence_similarity.png" \
        --p 50

             
jq -nc \
  --slurpfile c  "${doccano_dir}/combined_training_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json" \
  --slurpfile h1 "${doccano_dir}/training_hard_negatives_semantic_similarity_${RUN_TAG}.json" \
  --slurpfile h2 "${doccano_dir}/training_hard_negatives_matched_grep_${RUN_TAG}.json" '
  ($c[0] + $h1[0] + $h2[0]
    | map(if type == "string" then . else .text end
          | select(type == "string")
          | {(.): true})
    | add) as $keep
  | inputs
  | select($keep[.text // ""])
' "${doccano_dir}/combined_training_dedup_annotated_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl" |
awk '!seen[$0]++' > "${doccano_dir}/training_set.jsonl"      

echo "Total number of selected training sentences"
wc -l ${doccano_dir}/training_set.jsonl

echo "Number of selected training sentences, by type"
jq 'length' ${doccano_dir}/combined_training_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json \
      ${doccano_dir}/training_hard_negatives_semantic_similarity_${RUN_TAG}.json \
      ${doccano_dir}/training_hard_negatives_matched_grep_${RUN_TAG}.json

echo "Out of total possible training sentences"
jq 'length' ${doccano_dir}/combined_training_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json \
             ${doccano_dir}/combined_training_non_cohort_sentences_${RUN_TAG}.json
        
# ~35% of total possible sentences are selected

```

## Combine validation text: 

```{bash}

cd output/doccano

# combine training examples into a single jsonl file
# create new sentence id numbers 
jq -c  '.' \
  validation_title_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  validation_abstracts_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  validation_methods_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  validation_results_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
  validation_intros_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl \
| jq -c -s 'to_entries | map(.value + {orig_id: .value.id, id: (.key + 1)}) | .[]' \
  > combined_validation_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

# source_section identifies the section of the article from which the sentence was extracted, e.g. title, abstracts, methods, results, introduction, or full text (unknown section)
jq '
  . + {
    source_section:
      (if (.source_file | test("main"; "i")) then "full text (unknown section)"
       elif (.source_file | test("methods"; "i")) then "methods"
       elif (.source_file | test("results"; "i")) then "results"
       elif (.source_file | test("abstract"; "i")) then "abstract"
       elif (.source_file | test("title"; "i")) then "title"
       elif (.source_file | test("intro"; "i")) then "introduction"
       else null
       end)
  }
' combined_validation_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_validation_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl
  
# deduplicate combined validation examples based on pubmed_id and text, keeping the first occurrence of each unique combination, and reassigning ids
jq -c -s '
  reduce .[] as $r ({seen: {}, out: []};
    ($r.pubmed_id + "\u0000" + $r.text) as $k
    | if .seen[$k] then . else .seen[$k] = true | .out += [$r] end)
  | .out
  | to_entries | map(.value + {orig_id: .value.id, id: (.key + 1)}) | .[]
' combined_validation_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_validation_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl


# remove source_file and orig_id fields from combined_validation_dedup.jsonl
jq -c 'del(.source_file)' \
combined_validation_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_validation_dedup_simple_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

jq -c 'del(.orig_id)' \
combined_validation_dedup_simple_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl > combined_validation_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

rm combined_validation_dedup_simple_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl
rm combined_validation_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

wc -l combined_validation_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl combined_validation_dedup_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl

rm combined_validation_edit_${RUN_TAG}.jsonl
```
